source.title: From Indirect Object Identification to Syllogisms: Exploring Binary Mechanisms in Transformer Circuits

record.tranche_reason: The study examines GPT-2 small head 10.7 in syllogism tasks and argues that its role is broader than copying: in opposite syllogisms it suppresses an attended truth token as part of a negation mechanism. This refines how the head's role should be described, but does not test copy suppression on ordinary text or across the training distribution.
record.gate_note: The study reports head-specific ablation and QK/OV findings for syllogism prompts. General syllogism performance and circuit-faithfulness aggregates are not separate rows because they do not isolate head 10.7. Results cited from prior copy-suppression or IOI work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study reports new results on GPT-2 small head 10.7 (and other negative heads) on templated syllogism prompts. These include mean-ablation, path patching, a weights-based QK and OV analysis (W_U W_OV MLP0 W_E) and logit inspection. It also argues the heads' role should be restated as encoding the anti-direction in binary settings. The measured behaviour matches copy suppression: the head attends to the in-context truth token, which the truth heads predict, and pushes it to the bottom logits. The negation itself is done by downstream MLPs. Appendix D adds a result on negative heads in larger models.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses constructed syllogism prompts and path patching, QK/OV analysis, and logit-lens-style inspection. It does not test the original copy-suppression claim on ordinary text or report the original loss-attribution measure.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported role of head 10.7 changes across Simple, Opposite, and Complex Syllogism formats.
record.problems: Evidence is limited to templated syllogism tasks rather than ordinary text or the training distribution. Head-specific findings are mostly qualitative, and no uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No head-specific numerical values were left out. General circuit faithfulness and task-level average logit differences were omitted because they aggregate components or measure overall task performance rather than head 10.7's behavior.

untested.parts: Ordinary text and the training distribution. 'Mainly' is not quantified relative to other roles.
The share of the head's loss effect explained by QK/OV (76.9%). No ablation constrained to the mechanism.
Negative name movers in IOI are discussed but not re-measured. No GPT-2 sizes other than XL, and no per-head suppression analysis in the larger models.

versions.untested_parts: Ordinary text and the training distribution; whether the suppressed token is predicted by earlier components and also occurs earlier in context.
Whether the mechanism explains most of the head's effect on loss, including the 76.9% figure.
Whether negative name movers in IOI, or negative heads in other models and sizes, have the same role.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.value: Mean-ablating head 10.7 improves performance beyond the baseline
rows.locator: Section 3.1, Negative Heads in Simple Syllogism
rows.note: The result shows the head is not needed for this task's performance, but does not directly measure copy suppression.
rows.check: In SS the truth token is both present in context and predicted by the Truth Heads. Ablating 10.7 improves logit difference, which is what suppression of that token predicts. The evidence is indirect (no direct logit measure), and there is no numeric value. Linking to V5 is not needed; this is the same head.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.1, Negative Heads in Simple Syllogism

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Ablate attention head 10.7 using path patching
rows.value: Ablating head 10.7 leads to a significant drop in logit difference
rows.note: The text reports a significant drop but gives no head-specific numeric value.
rows.check: This shows only that 10.7 is causally important in OS. It does not show whether it suppresses, and no head-specific number is given (Figure 3b only). The baseline is the clean-run logit difference (OS average 1.2123).

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Inspect head 10.7's QK attention scores on opposite-syllogism prompts
rows.note: The authors describe the negative truth heads as consistently attending to the truth-value token.
rows.check: The scores are raw QK attention scores in vocabulary space. The query 'is' attending to key 'true' is the token the model would predict, which is consistent with the copy-suppression QK story. These are qualitative top pairs, not a quantitative QK test. The V5 link is dropped: this is the original head.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Inspect head 10.7's OV output and resulting logits
rows.measure: Position of truth-value tokens in the logits
rows.value: After OV from head 10.7, truth tokens do not rank highly; the text says negative truth heads suppress the truth token into the bottom logits
rows.locator: Table 3 and Section 3.2, Negative Truth Heads
rows.note: The associated MLP then promotes the opposite token; the study characterizes this as a negation pathway, not as ordinary-context copy suppression.
rows.check: The OV projection through the MLP0-extended embedding puts true/True/TRUE/untrue in the bottom logits (Table 3). This is the weights-based OV suppression that V2 names, and V1's suppression of an in-context token. The 'resulting logits' after MLP10 belong to the MLP, not the head.

source_check.locator_found: Table 3; Section 3.2, Negative Truth Heads and Mechanistic Interpretation

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Inspect head 10.7's attention and logit effects on complex-syllogism prompts
rows.measure: Attention to truth tokens and suppression behavior
rows.value: Head 10.7 attends to both truth tokens, places greater emphasis on the incorrect redundant truth token, and continues to suppress as described for Negative Truth Heads
rows.note: The result concerns a constructed syllogism with a misleading redundant statement, not ordinary text.
rows.check: This row covers 9.7, 10.7 and 11.10 jointly: they attend more to the incorrect redundant truth token and suppress it. The evidence is qualitative text only.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 small, templated simple, opposite and complex syllogism prompts
relationships.reason: 10.7 suppresses the attended in-context truth token (r4, r5), and ablating it improves SS logit difference, where that token is the correct answer (r1). The authors frame this as negation, but the head's own action is suppression; the MLP flips it.
relationships.display_finding: Head 10.7 suppressed the attended truth token, and ablating it improved SS logit difference when that token was correct; the MLP reversed the head’s suppression.

relation.reason: The study directly intervenes on head 10.7 and examines its QK, OV, attention and logit effects.

tranche.reason: Sections 3–4 present new interventions and mechanistic analysis, and argue for a broader interpretation of negative heads as participating in binary negation.

source_check.notes: Changes in task usefulness do not establish a reversal of the suppression operation. MLP-mediated negation is asymmetric: false inputs often remain false (Section 3.2). Cross-study counts and exclusivity claims were outside this study-only check.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Simple, opposite, and complex syllogism prompts
reader_labels.reason: Head 10.7 is not needed for simple-syllogism performance, while it supports opposite-syllogism logit difference and suppresses truth tokens in the opposite and complex formats; these task-dependent findings do not establish one role across the training distribution (r1, r2, r4, r5).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The study reports truth-token attention and suppression through head 10.7's OV output, followed by an MLP promoting the opposite token (r3, r4).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The study interprets head 10.7's opposite-syllogism behavior as part of a negation mechanism rather than simply copying the attended token, and its effect differs between simple and opposite tasks (r1, r2, r4, r5).
